hero_kpi_rationale: The cloud computing segment, particularly with AI infrastructure (AIC) and compute-to-edge, is the primary driver of future growth, aligned with the AI wave and demand for low-latency applications.

kpis.name: Cloud Backlog (CCB)
kpis.explanation: Future commitments related to cloud solutions, a leading indicator of upcoming revenue.
kpis.description: The cloud backlog reflects growing demand for distributed computing platforms and AI infrastructure services.
kpis.signal: Strong cloud backlog growth, indicating traction in new compute and AI services.

kpis.name: AI / Cloud Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from cloud and AI infrastructure solutions, key to the company's transformation.
kpis.description: Cloud computing and AI-related revenues include AIC and compute-to-edge solutions, experiencing strong expansion.
kpis.signal: Very strong growth in cloud and AI segment, the main engine of future trajectory.

kpis.name: Security Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from cybersecurity solutions, Akamai's current core segment.
kpis.description: Security solutions (WAF, Zero Trust, bot management) remain the core of revenue, with sustained growth.
kpis.signal: Security remains the leader, but growth is moderate compared to cloud/IA.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Consolidated gross margin, reflecting operational efficiency.
kpis.description: Gross margin is improving due to optimization of bandwidth and co-location costs.
kpis.signal: Gross margin improvement driven by better network cost management.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin declined slightly due to investments in compute-to-edge deployment.
kpis.signal: Slight pressure on operating margin despite revenue growth.

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Share of research and development expenses in total revenue.
kpis.description: Akamai is increasing R&D spending to accelerate innovation on distributed infrastructure platforms.
kpis.signal: R&D up to strengthen cloud and AI offerings.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures (CAPEX)
kpis.explanation: Investments in fixed assets to expand network and computing infrastructure.
kpis.description: CAPEX investments support the expansion of the distributed compute network and points of presence.
kpis.signal: CAPEX rising sharply to deploy compute-to-edge and AI infrastructure.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Akamai is streamlining headcount while maintaining innovation on key products.
kpis.signal: Slight reduction in headcount to improve productivity.

kpis.name: Percentage of deals including AI features
kpis.explanation: Percentage of new cloud contracts that include artificial intelligence capabilities.
kpis.description: 35% of new cloud contracts in 2025 include AI components, up from 25% in 2024.
kpis.signal: Rapid adoption of AI in new cloud deals.

kpis.name: Volume of AI API calls
kpis.explanation: Number of calls to artificial intelligence APIs for threat detection and automation.
kpis.description: The volume of AI API calls has more than doubled, driven by generative AI usage in cybersecurity.
kpis.signal: Explosion in AI API calls, indicating deep adoption.

risks.title: Limited revenue growth and pricing pressure
risks.score_rationale: Revenue growth could slow or decline due to competition, pricing pressure on delivery solutions, and customer DIY initiatives reducing reliance on Akamai services.

risks.title: Geopolitical and macroeconomic risks
risks.score_rationale: Global geopolitical conditions and macroeconomic challenges could reduce customer spending by optimizing traffic, directly impacting Akamai's revenue and profitability.

risks.title: Infrastructure cost management challenges
risks.score_rationale: Co-location and bandwidth costs are rising significantly due to market pressures from hyperscalers. The expansion of the compute platform requires substantial investment with uncertain utilization.

risks.title: Cybersecurity risks and infrastructure dependency
risks.score_rationale: As a provider of critical internet infrastructure, a disruption or compromise of systems could have a catastrophic impact on Akamai's customers and operations.

risks.title: Challenges integrating recent acquisitions
risks.score_rationale: Akamai has acquired several assets (Fermyon, Edgio, Noname Security) whose successful integration is critical to realizing expected synergies and growing the cloud/IA portfolio.

risks.title: Increasing capital expenditures and depreciation
risks.score_rationale: Growing investments in compute infrastructure and network equipment generate significant depreciation, compressing operating margins despite revenue growth.

ai_positioning.summary: Akamai positions AI as a core element of its strategy, integrating generative AI and adaptive AI into its security, compute, and infrastructure solutions. The company offers cloud infrastructure platforms for building AI-powered applications, as well as AI-enhanced cybersecurity services using generative AI for threat detection.
evidence: Compute platform with AI infrastructure (AIC) and compute-to-edge
Cybersecurity solutions powered by adaptive AI and automation
Generative AI to accelerate identification and investigation of malicious activities
Global network infrastructure to support AI-powered applications
35% of new cloud contracts include AI components in 2025
